newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MENOTTI VICTORIOUS IN COACHES' GRUDGE MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MENOTTI VICTORIOUS IN COACHES' GRUDGE MATCH.

text.p: Cesar Luis Menotti emerged victorious on Sunday as his Independiente team beat Carlos Bilardo's Boca Juniors in an encounter seen as a grudge match between Argentina's two World Cup winning coaches.
Menotti not only robbed his great rival of a last chance to stay in the race for the Argentine Apertura championship but also pushed him one step nearer the sack.

The 1-0 defeat, in a match played in Boca's Bombonera stadium, means it is now nearly impossible for Boca to win the title, something seen as almost obligatory after they spent $15 million on assembling their team.
Boca, who have already been eliminated from the South American Supercup, are eleven points behind leaders River Plate with only nine matches to play.
It was the first time for 23 years that teams coached by the pair had clashed.

Menotti, who led Argentina to World Cup victory in 1978, and Bilardo, triumphant in 1986, have worked for the same cause in the past but they have entirely different views on how the game should be played and share a bitter personal rivalry.
Bilardo is known for favouring a win-at-all-costs approach while Menotti prefers his teams to play with style and panache.

Boca had the best of the first half but fell apart after defender Nestor Fabbri was sent off in the 60th minute for a second bookable offence. Six minutes later Francisco Guerrero scored the winner to keep Independiente second in the table.
Boca later had Nestor Lorenzo sent off for dissent while Independiente's Pablo Rotchen was given the red card for chopping down Boca's Cameroon striker Alphonse Tchami from behind.
River, the reigning South American champions, maintained a three-point advantage in the tournament, the first of two championships played in the Argentine season, with a 1-0 win over Estudiantes.
Unfashionable Lanus beat San Lorenzo 3-1 to stay third, trailing Independiente on goal difference.
